title: Heatmap Ops Corridor Sync — correlation sweep and runbook draft
body:
Meeting: Heatmap Ops Corridor sync — ad-hoc series to find signal->latency correlations
Date: 2026-11-03
Owner: Asha Patel (notes)
Attendees: Miguel, Leah, Jonas, Priya, Asha (partial)

Agenda:
- Quick recap of last week's shadow-run anomalies (QPS valleys at 14:12-14:22 UTC)
- Present heatmap correlation sweep results (Leah)
- Triage hypotheses + decide runbook steps and owners
- Repro plan and guardrails for canary tests

Summary (TL;DR):
- Heatmap intensity across serving nodes shows a consistent corridor pattern that precedes 95th/99th latency spikes by ~15–45s in three isolated incidents during shadow runs.
- Preliminary correlation coefficient between corridor intensity (normalized per-node) and p95 latency = 0.62 over last 48h sample; stronger (0.74) when filtering runs with seq_len >= 512.
- Top hypotheses: (A) KV-cache eviction storms during mixed-seq batches; (B) batch packing causing microstarvation on hot GPU SMs; (C) intermittent GC/housekeeping on sidecar agents; (D) NUMA-related slowdown on certain host types.

Observations and raw signals (Leah):
- Heatmap metric: serving.node.token_density_heatmap_bucket_{i} (normalized), shown aggregated into a corridor score (0-1).
- Corridor rises steadily for 10-30s before tail latency jump in ~80% of incidents we examined.
- KV-cache_hit_rate drops 6–12% during corridor ramp; memory_free on host drops ~200–600MB in those windows.
- GPU SM utilization has small oscillations (~5–8%) but not a complete drop; CPU steal increases on host by ~3–5% in two incidents.
- Network queues (cni tx drops) were present in 1/7 samples but not common.

Representative run excerpt (timestamps UTC):
- 2026-11-02T14:12:09Z corridor_score 0.12 p95 86ms qps 980
- 2026-11-02T14:12:24Z corridor_score 0.54 p95 140ms qps 870 (kv_cache_hit 0.88 -> 0.80)
- 2026-11-02T14:12:36Z corridor_score 0.87 p95 332ms qps 760 (batch packing spikes, active batches 2 -> 5)
- 2026-11-02T14:12:57Z corridor_score 0.20 p95 92ms qps 1020 (recovered)

Quick triage notes (Jonas):
- KV-cache eviction hypothesis: eviction traces show LRU churn during heavy mixed seq runs; prefix cache size saw transient drops. Eviction is correlated in time, plausible root cause.
- Batch packing: our packing heuristic allows mixing a 1024 seq with many 64s — leads to larger batches occasionally; packing latency slightly higher when packing count > 4.
- Agent GC: sidecars running python-based metrics collector had a correlated GC pause (saw SIGSTOP-like pause in process for ~120–300ms) in two out of seven runs. Need to confirm with more traces.
- NUMA: one affected host (ip-10-2-14-77) shows nonideal memory locality during prime window; slabs show higher remote access rates.

Experiment & reproduction plan (short):
1) Targeted shadow-run with filters: seq_len buckets {<=64, 65-256, 257-1024}, forcing mixed packing ratios and enabling kv-cache debug logging. (Owner: Miguel) -- run by 2026-11-05
   - Command prototype: ./bench/run_shadow.sh --model gptx-small --qps 1000 --seq-profile mixed --trace-kvcache --pack-debug > run.out
2) Sidecar GC instrumentation: bump metrics-agent GC logging and collect flamegraphs for collector process during runs (Owner: Leah) -- by 2026-11-04
3) Constrain batch packing in a canary: set max_pack_items=3 on a small subset and compare tail-latency with control (Owner: Priya) -- canary start 2026-11-06
4) NUMA isolation test: run suspect load on node pinned to a single NUMA zone vs default; compare remote access counters (Owner: Jonas) -- by 2026-11-07

Preliminary runbook draft (what on-call should check):
- If corridor_score > 0.6 and p95 rise > 50ms:
  - Check kv-cache hit rate and recent eviction logs (path: /var/log/kvcache/evictions.log).
  - Check metrics-agent uptime and recent GC logs (/var/log/metrics-agent/gc.log).
  - If agent GC detected, drain node, replace with new sidecar build (temp fix).
  - If eviction heavy, temporarily raise prefix_cache bytes for that pool by +20% via config (requires rollout).
  - If NUMA remote accesses > 10% increase, mark host for NUMA test and avoid scheduling new canaries.

Data needs & dashboards (Leah):
- Add corridor_score to per-route dashboard (overlay p95/p99, kv-cache_hit_rate, mem_free, pack_count)
- Spike explore: heatmap -> show per-node corridor overlay and ability to click into trace ids (link to traces prepopulated)
- Add an alert preview: corridor_score > 0.7 sustained 20s AND p95 > 150ms -> page SRE on-call as P3.

Open questions / risks:
- Are cache evictions symptomatic (downstream of packing) or causal? Need controlled runs with cache disabled to see tail impact.
- Is the metrics-agent GC due to max-open sockets or leak after prolonged shadow runs?
- Risk of raising prefix_cache: will increase memory pressure and could shift the problem to other nodes. Need ephemeral canary config.
- Any interplay with our autoscaler warmup logic that throttles container startup during corridor windows? (suspected once)

Decisions made in meeting:
- Proceed with targeted shadow-run (Miguel) and sidecar GC instrumentation (Leah) in parallel.
- Don't roll global prefix_cache change without canary evidence.
- Prepare a short playbook (this doc -> convert to Confluence page) before any config tweak. (Owner: Asha)

Action items (owners + dates):
- Miguel: run filtered shadow-run with kv-cache debug logs and pack ratios by 2026-11-05 (deliver: run artifacts + sample traces)
- Leah: enable GC flamegraphs for metrics-agent; collect 3 successful traces and 3 incident traces by 2026-11-04
- Priya: prepare canary config for max_pack_items=3 and rehearse rollback steps by 2026-11-05
- Jonas: schedule NUMA isolation test on ip-10-2-14-77 and report counters by 2026-11-07
- Asha: migrate this doc to Confluence as 'Heatmap Corridor playbook v0.1' and link alerts by 2026-11-06

Notes to self / heuristics: (informal)
- When reproducing, try to seed with a work-mix of 10% long prompts (>1k) + 70% short interactive + 20% embeddings. Long prompts seem to prime corridor.
- Keep a tiny buffer in prefix cache for shadow nodes (+10MB) not global.
- If packing limit helps in canary, consider dynamic pack limit based on recent corridor_score.

Appendix: quick commands and traces to pull
- pull traces: ./infra/trace_util.sh fetch --time "2026-11-02T14:10:00Z" --time-end "2026-11-02T14:20:00Z" --filter corridor_score>0.4 > traces-1412.json
- capture flamegraph: kubectl exec -it metrics-agent -- /usr/local/bin/collect-flame --duration 60 --out /tmp/fg.svg
- shadow run: ./bench/runner --config confs/mixed-pack-1.json --qps 1000 --duration 600 --enable-kv-trace

If you can't reproduce locally, attach full run artifacts and we will triage in bench-sync next Wed.

---
If anything missing, add to this doc. Will update after first shadow run results come in.
